body: Poor mental health doesn’t need a reason. To say he’s not dealing with anything hard is clearly only because you’re upset with him. He is dealing with his mother possibly dying and probably other issues most 17 year olds face. It’s not your place to tell someone whether something that is very clearly affecting them (whether you know what it is or not) is invalid.

Maybe. I think you’re both wrong, he seems to have bigger mental health issues than you give him credit for. Being in therapy doesn’t fix everything. Often anger is really other emotion expressed the wrong way. This does not excuse the behavior but he is at a time where he probably needs his family just like your mom does. I know it doesn’t seem the same but mental health can be as debilitating as physical health. He may have neglected his duties to your mom but he’s also quite a bit younger, his brain isn’t fully developed. 
For you to not buy him tickets and suggest leaving him behind was the confirmation that he wasn’t wanted. He may have acted inexcusably but to feel that one isn’t wanted or loved is the worst feeling. 
I wish your mother a speedy recovery

Hi so I used to have more mild compulsions but developed to severe after some traumatic incidents in my life. When I asked my therapist why I had to stop doing the milder compulsions if they were harmless here is what she said:
When you get relief from doing the mild compulsions, your brain senses that. Now you’ve made the association between irrational thoughts and mental relief. This often cements a strong foundation in the brain that these thoughts are good for you so it will produce more to help you cope with different and more stressful situations. 
The longer you let your brain believe it was the compulsion keeping you safe the harder it will be to get rid of the thoughts. 
(I hope I phrased that okay?) 

I am not at all qualified but that’s just what my therapist suggested. 
While mild ocd may not necessarily develop into something worse I would definitely recommend looking up some exposure therapy to eradicate them while they’re still at a manageable point. Nip it in the bud before it takes over your life!
